title: Bounded result JSON retains host compatibility and projection responsibilities
observed_need: Expose a stable result document to mncs-actions and future Forge without losing typed native values or structured diagnostics.
current_language_behavior: Native assertions, suite verdicts, retained execution values, process-outcome classification, subprocess-fallback execution adjudication, the family-check path CheckResult policy projection, bounded run_id plus per-test lineage digests, per-test canonical execution/observation JSON construction for ordinary bounded string/null fields, ArtifactStore payload/file digests through 65,536 bytes, and public result JSON formatting for bounded JSON value trees are MNCS-owned. The run-identity app constructs canonical JSON for bounded inputs; Python projects typed identity fields and retains compact-JSON compatibility for out-of-contract inputs. The result-identity batch app handles up to 16 payloads, 64 chunks, 65,536 bytes, and the 8,000,000-step limit. The stream app carries native SHA-256 state across ArtifactStore calls of at most 12,288 bytes each and at most six calls per artifact. Larger ArtifactStore content retains the host streaming hashlib compatibility path because repeated native application launches caused excessive process fan-out on real multi-megabyte compiler artifacts. Python reads files, sends bounded chunks, writes artifacts, supervises processes, and retains host source/provenance hashing; the Rust bootstrap CLI retains its JSON and artifact boundaries. The public serializer sorts object keys, escapes and indents values, and emits the trailing newline. Documents through 16,300 bytes use the single-call application; documents through 32,684 bytes use up to 32 continuation calls of at most 8,192 JSON bytes each. Pages may stop before a whole value when its conservative size bound would cross the page limit, leaving page capacity unused; the window application carries native SHA-256 state across pages.
why_insufficient: The bounded public serializer accepts at most 512 values, depth 63, 64 children per object, 256-byte keys, 1,024-byte scalar text, and 32,684 output bytes. Larger or unsupported values retain the compatibility path. Python still performs typed value projection, reassembles native UTF-8-safe pages, and writes public documents. ArtifactStore native streaming is capped at 65,536 bytes: the 20,000-byte payload/file differential test used four native app executions. Before this cap, the runner self-suite exposed compiler artifacts around 13 MB and remained active at 5:43 with repeated stream-app execution; a file of that size would require more than 1,000 launches at 12,288 bytes per call. Larger artifact hashes therefore retain the host streaming hashlib path until the native runtime can consume large inputs without one process launch per window. With the cap and compatibility boundary in place, the integrated self-suite passed in 184.69 seconds. The complete cross-repository evidence protocol and out-of-contract run-identity projection remain outside the native application surface. Python also retains typed value projection, filesystem access, source/provenance hashes, and compatibility behavior for unsupported or over-bound inputs. The Rust bootstrap CLI retains its JSON and artifact boundaries.
minimal_reproducer: tools/mncs_test.py::_public_result_json_payload receives a result requiring more than 16,300 output bytes, projects its JSON value tree, invokes test-public-result-json-window in continuation pages, and carries SHA-256 state through the window application. tests/test_public_result_json.py::test_native_json_supports_results_larger_than_legacy_window compares emitted bytes and digest to independent Python JSON and SHA-256 results, including a UTF-8 scalar at an output chunk boundary. tests/test_artifact_hashing.py::test_artifact_store_streams_medium_payload_and_file_hashes_in_mncs compares 20,000-byte payload and file digests to independent hashlib results while confirming the host hash functions are not called; test_artifact_store_bounds_native_streaming_to_64_kib verifies larger inputs do not trigger per-window application fan-out. Python still projects typed runtime and identity values and retains compatibility behavior for unsupported or over-bound inputs.
desired_direction: Extend the bounded native serializer and streaming identity capabilities through real consumers, while moving common text, collection, and typed-value projection mechanisms into reusable MNCS stdlib interfaces where migration requirements support them. Keep application policy and platform filesystem/process access at their existing ownership boundaries.
workaround: The MNCS test-check-result-projection application owns CheckResult policy and reference construction; test-lineage-identity constructs and hashes ordinary per-test execution/observation JSON; test-run-identity constructs and hashes bounded canonical run identities; test-result-identity hashes bounded payload batches; test-result-identity-stream carries native SHA-256 state to hash ArtifactStore payloads and files through 65,536 bytes in at most six 12,288-byte windows; larger artifact content uses the host streaming hashlib compatibility path to avoid excessive process launches; test-public-result-json serializes small bounded results, and test-public-result-json-window serializes larger bounded values while carrying SHA-256 state across pages through mncs.std.sha256.v1. The adapter respects native row, field, payload, page, byte, step, and stream-call limits, retains compatibility behavior outside them, and independently checks the final public-document digest. Python still projects typed values, reassembles unresolved-message and JSON pages, performs filesystem access, hashes source/provenance files, and serializes unsupported or over-bound public values. It also retains process supervision, raw diagnostic transport, and explicit Actions/compatibility transport; it no longer classifies subprocess transport or decoded execution outcomes.
